fixes.explanation: Oil on the head sounds fancy, friend, like a spa day under the oaks. But oil isn't in Abraham's offer. He says, “Let a little water be brought, that you may wash your feet and rest yourselves under the tree.” (Genesis 18:4). Water for washing and a tree to rest under. That's what he puts on the table first.

Honey! Okay, I see you, baker. You're thinking like somebody who has stood in front of a cooling rack. But Abraham says, “And I will bring a bit of bread so that you may refresh yourselves.” (Genesis 18:5). Bread is the word he uses, and he even calls it a bit. Hold on to that word, because this meal is about to grow.

problems.problem: The text does not say the visitors had tired feet. Calling water and shade the whole offer also overlooks Abraham’s offer of bread in verse 5.
The text says Abraham offered bread, but does not say it was plain.
